clue.text: Bits of food terrible, about to be eaten — gosh!

indicators.note: something eaten goes inside the eater, so the word for about sits within the word for terrible

parts.note: terrible means bad
re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
crumbs is a mild exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone complains that food scraps look awful and are about to be eaten, then exclaims in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs are tiny broken pieces, here of a loaf, so this is a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Managed to come before king in status

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business, gives ran
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A manager rising above the king in standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank is one's position or standing in a hierarchy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wild person at party losing head, say

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a raver is someone who parties wildly

explanation.surface: A partygoer gets decapitated, so to speak, in mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert, so it can stand for say as a verb.

clue.text: Strange dialect in SA hall

definitions.note: SA is the Salvation Army, whose meeting halls are called by this military name

indicators.note: strange letters are oddly arranged, prompting a rearrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: An odd accent heard in a hall in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SA looks like South Africa but stands for the Salvation Army, which names its places of worship after fortresses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army uses military terms, and its local worship building is called a fortress name.

clue.text: Chemical stuck in your ears

indicators.note: the letters are lodged within the phrase that follows, across the word gap

explanation.surface: Some substance has got lodged in your ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a nitrogen compound found in urine, so it is an example of a chemical.

clue.text: By carrying torch, maybe, you can see home from afar

indicators.note: one word carries the other inside it, holding it within

parts.note: a torch is an example of a light, hence the maybe

explanation.surface: With a torch to hand you can spot your house from a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTY is old soldiers' slang for Britain, used by those serving abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: British servicemen overseas called their homeland by this slang name, so it is home seen from far away.

clue.text: Tudor yeomen looking silly in old book

indicators.note: the words appear in a foolish disarray, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sixteenth-century yeomen appear foolish in some antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifth book of the Old Testament, so a book of great age.

clue.text: Generate din, going mad as one sort of actress

indicators.note: the letters go crazy and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: An actress making a racket and losing her mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a woman who acts in serious dramas, a particular kind of stage performer.

clue.text: Heartless denier of his friend, look

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Saint Peter denied knowing Jesus three times before the cock crowed

explanation.surface: A cruel man who betrayed his friend, told to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely or with difficulty, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: An attractive number

parts.note: aesthetic can mean tasteful or pleasing to the eye

explanation.surface: A good-looking girl, or a catchy song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure or a song: read it as something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that deadens feeling is literally a numb-er, a thing that numbs.

clue.text: Don't hunt him with dogs — bring back the guns!

indicators.note: bringing back the word means reading it from its end to its start

parts.note: gats is old American slang for pistols

explanation.surface: An anti-hunting protest that ends, oddly, by demanding the guns return.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: this deer is the quarry of hound hunts, which campaigners oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: The male deer was traditionally hunted with hounds, so it is the animal not to chase that way.

clue.text: Seabirds needing rare wash set out

indicators.note: set out means arranged differently, so these letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Birds of the sea in need of an unusual laundering.
explanation.definitionFit: These are ocean birds that skim the waves, related to petrels.

clue.text: A nasty smell on road — country thing that's disgusting

parts.note: BO is body odour
MI is the M1, Britain's first motorway
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A dreadful stink on the highway: a disgusting national affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An object of loathing or disgust; the word means a vile or detestable thing.

clue.text: Proceeded with difficulty, kitchen device having leaked

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface on a stove
bled means lost fluid, leaked out

explanation.surface: A cook struggles on after a stove appliance starts leaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp along awkwardly is to walk with difficulty, the sense of the verb.

clue.text: Old Italian smoker died making ascent

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Etna is the smoking volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian who smoked died, his soul rising.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval poet of the Divine Comedy was a Florentine, so an Italian from long ago.

clue.text: The German scoundrels returning took leading roles

indicators.note: turning back means the letters are read from the end

parts.note: der is a German word for the
rats are scoundrels

explanation.surface: German villains come back and grab the main parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who played the lead were the stars of the show, the past tense of that verb.

clue.text: Animal rested before getting tucked in

indicators.note: one word is tucked inside the other

parts.note: sat means rested on a seat
to means before, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: A creature had a rest before being put to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small carnivorous mammal of the weasel family, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Unprofessional types showing sloppiness, but don't get cross!

indicators.note: not getting the item means it is left out of the word

parts.note: laxity means slackness or sloppiness
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: Amateurs being slapdash, told not to lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary people as opposed to clergy or professionals form this group.

clue.text: Causes 'urt to members

definitions.meaning: in a dropped-h Cockney accent, harms becomes '..., matching hurts with its h dropped
limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: Someone with a dropped-h accent complains of injuries to their limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'urt signals a dropped h, so the matching verb for damages loses its h too.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper limbs are bodily members; and a Cockney's version of harms.

clue.text: Work needed — this joint has got restricted

indicators.note: the letters are confined within the words, held inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A joint that has stiffened up and needs treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg's hinge between thigh and shin is a joint, so it is an example.

clue.text: Book a sailor brought back

indicators.note: bringing it back means reading the word backwards

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman returns with a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of maps is a kind of book.

clue.text: A good lot of drinks gets one unable to move somehow

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: A good round of drinks leaves someone unable to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the bottom cannot move; the adjective describes being stranded.

clue.text: Something unpleasant in bag is a resin

indicators.note: one word sits in the other

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
hell is any very unpleasant experience

explanation.surface: A nasty surprise found inside a bag turns out to be sticky gum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a resin secreted by the lac insect, used for varnish.

clue.text: Money for job when worker is in town

indicators.note: the worker is placed in the middle of the pay word

parts.note: a wage is pay for work
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Pay for a job when a labourer is in town.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTAGE is a market town in Oxfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Oxfordshire market town is an example of a town.

clue.text: Is yours truly coming in skinny? Organic substance needed

indicators.note: the phrase comes into the other word

parts.note: skinny means thin
said by the speaker, is yours truly becomes I am

explanation.surface: A thin person asks whether they themselves need some nutrient.
explanation.definitionFit: This is vitamin B1, an organic compound the body needs.

clue.text: Famous South African in a short skirt

definitions.meaning: Desmond ... was the Nobel-winning archbishop of Cape Town
the stiff short skirt worn by a ballerina

explanation.surface: A famous South African wearing a little skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The archbishop Desmond shares his surname with a ballet dancer's frilly skirt.

clue.text: Run away briefly when meeting a bloodsucker

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to flee is to run away

explanation.surface: Running off quickly on encountering a vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: This jumping insect feeds on blood, so it is a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Big sound from the heart? Not the heart

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the central letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: the bosom is the breast, seat of the feelings

explanation.surface: A loud noise comes from the chest, then a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep resonant noise such as thunder is a loud sound.

clue.text: Writer said to be a founder of state

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for a writer is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author is reputed to have founded a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: William Penn founded the colony of Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: William Penn established the American colony that became Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Vigorous and in no need of a transfusion?

definitions.text: in no need of a transfusion?
definitions.meaning: playfully, a body already brimming with blood

explanation.surface: A robust patient who obviously needs no extra blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means hearty and committed, and literally suggests a body with plenty of blood.

clue.text: Cross and offensive, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the clue asks us to hear the word for offensive

parts.note: rude means offensive

explanation.surface: Someone angry and insulting, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

clue.text: Promotion from publicists not ultimately enthralling Packard

indicators.note: holding something captive within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: admen are advertising people
Vance Packard wrote The Hidden Persuaders about advertising

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Advertisers fail to captivate Packard, their famous critic, so no promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting promoted is advancing in rank, a synonym.
